desc: Derive the correct minimum-moves formula: prove that with required visits need[i] = ceil(T/points[i]), setting v[n-1]=need[n-1] and v[i]=max(need[i], v[i+1]) yields min moves = 2*sum(v) - v[n-1] - 1 (or equivalent), and validate against examples and brute force on small cases.
Implement check(T) in O(n) using the derived formula, being careful with large numbers (m up to 1e9, points up to 1e6, so visits up to ~1e15 — use Python ints, fine).
Implement binary search over answer in [0, upper_bound] where upper_bound accounts for total score concentrateable on one cell (~ m * max(points) bounded appropriately).

Run the full binary search on the two samples to confirm outputs 4 and 2, and stress-test the greedy check against a brute-force BFS/DP on small random cases (including n=2 with huge m and points[i]=1 bottleneck cases).
Test edge cases (n=2 with m=1, large m, equal points) and finalize complexity analysis.
Write final solution in the starter code format with imports and typing.
